reason: Holding beats trading because the book's core thesis got stronger this week and nothing on it is broken. Web research (search worked) shows the Fed in a hiking cycle at 3.75-4.00% after the September hike. The September FOMC minutes say most participants see another hike as likely by year end; UOB expects December 2026 and 1Q 2027 hikes, and futures price about an 80% hold for the 28 Oct meeting after a weak September jobs report. Each hike lifts the coupons on the 66% AAA CLO floater sleeve (JAAA 50%, ICLO 16%), while the engine's cash rate stays at 4%, which is the carry this book is built to harvest. All four legs are positive since the 2026-09-30 entry: JAAA +0.12%, ICLO +0.12%, AMLP +1.33%, SPYI +1.73%. No stop is near (the floaters have -8% stops against near-zero price volatility), and no standing orders fired on this book in the stop-out wave that hit leveraged and high-beta names this week. I found no current AAA CLO spread data or 2026 midstream news, so the AMLP and spread views rest on the packet marks rather than fresh reporting. A replacement would cost real basis points to get back roughly the same exposures. Risk to watch: a growth scare that flips the Fed to cuts would cut floater coupons; I would reassess the floater weight then, not now.
